chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah from his father from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said:

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام was brought a man who had killed another man by mistake. So ʿAlī عليه السلام said, “Who are your clan and your relatives?” He said, “I have no relatives or clan in this town.” He said, “From the people of which towns are you?” He said, “I am a man from the people of al-Mawṣil. I was born there, and I have relatives and a household there.” Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn inquired about him, but found that he had no relatives or clan for him in al-Kūfah.

He said: So he wrote to his governor over al-Mawṣil: “To proceed: so-and-so son of so-and-so, whose description is such-and-such, killed a Muslim man by mistake, and he has stated that he is a man from the people of al-Mawṣil and that he has relatives and a household there. I have sent him to you with my messenger, so-and-so son of so-and-so, whose description is such-and-such. So when they arrive to you, if Allah wills, and you have read my letter, investigate his matter and ask about his relatives among the Muslims. If he is from the people of al-Mawṣil, from those born there, and you find for him there relatives from among the Muslims, then gather them to you. Then look: if there is there a man who inherits from him, having a share in the Book, whom none of his relatives bars from his inheritance, then obligate him to the blood money and exact it from him over three years. And if he has no relative having a share in the Book, and his relatives are equal in lineage, then distribute the blood money over his relatives from his father’s side and his relatives from his mother’s side, from among the adult Muslim men. Then place upon his relatives from his father’s side two-thirds of the blood money, and place upon his relatives from his mother’s side one-third of the blood money. And if he has no relatives from his mother’s side, then distribute the blood money over his relatives from his father’s side from among the adult Muslim men. Then exact it from them and seek payment of the blood money from them over three years. And if he has no relatives from his father’s side and no relatives from his mother’s side, then distribute the blood money over the people of al-Mawṣil from among those born there and raised there, and do not include among them others from the people of the towns. Then seek that from them over three years, in each year an instalment, until you receive it in full, if Allah wills. And if so-and-so son of so-and-so has no relatives from the people of al-Mawṣil, and he is not from its people, and he is making a false claim, then send him back to me with my messenger, so-and-so son of so-and-so, if Allah wills; for I am his guardian and the one who pays on his behalf, and the blood of a Muslim man is not to be left without recompense.”

key_terms.خَطَأً: by mistake; accidental rather than intentional killing
key_terms.سَهْمٌ فِي ٱلْكِتَابِ: a fixed inheritance share established in the Book of Allah
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his guardian with legal authority over his matter
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةَ: blood money due for unlawful killing
key_terms.ٱلرِّجَالِ ٱلْمُدْرِكِينَ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ: adult Muslim men legally counted for liability
key_terms.ٱلْمُودِي عَنْهُ: the one who pays the blood money on his behalf

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the diyyah in accidental killing if the killer has no local relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام concerning liability for blood money in a case of accidental killing. It sets out the order of financial responsibility among the killer’s inheriting kin, wider male relatives, local people of his place of origin, and finally the Imam as guardian, affirming that the blood of a Muslim is not to be neglected.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5308 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn Atiyyah from his father from Salamah ibn Kuhayl who said: A man who had killed another man by mistake was brought to Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as).

Imam Ali (as) asked him: "Who are your relatives and kin?"
The man replied: "I have no relatives or kin in this town."
Imam Ali (as) then asked: "From which town are you?"
The man said: "I am a man from Mosul. I was born there and have relatives and family there."
Imam Ali (as) inquired about him but found that he had no relatives or kin in Kufa.
So, Imam Ali (as) wrote to his governor in Mosul:
"After the greeting, so-and-so (mentioning his name and description) has killed a Muslim man by mistake. He claims that he is a man from Mosul and has relatives and family there.

I have sent him to you with my messenger (mentioning his name and description). When they arrive, God willing, and you read my letter, investigate his situation and inquire about his Muslim relatives.
If he indeed belongs to Mosul, was born there, and you find that he has relatives among the Muslims, gather them together. Then, if there is a man among them who inherits from him with a rightful share in the Book (of Allah (swt)) and is not barred from his inheritance by any other relative, obligate him to pay the blood money (diyyah) over the course of three years.
If the deceased has a relative who is entitled to inherit according to the Book (Qur'an), then obligate that heir to pay the blood money (diyyah) over three years.
However, if he has no relative entitled to inheritance from his family, and his relatives are equal in lineage, then distribute the blood money (diyyah) equally among his paternal and maternal male relatives who are adults and Muslims.
Assign two-thirds of the blood money to his paternal relatives and one-third to his maternal relatives. If he has no maternal relatives, distribute the entire blood money among his paternal male relatives who are adults and Muslims. Collect the blood money from them over three years.
If he has neither paternal nor maternal relatives, distribute the blood money among the people of Mosul who were born and raised there, and do not include anyone else from other regions. Collect the amount from them over three years in annual instalments until the full amount is paid, God willing.
However, if so-and-so has no relatives in Mosul and is not from its people, and his claim is false, then send him back to me with my messenger, so-and-so, God willing. I am his guardian and responsible for paying his blood money, and the blood of a Muslim cannot be disregarded."
